title: Segmented CUDA-Graph capture strategy for tiled KV + attention-fusion to reduce transient replay failures
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: We intermittently observe CUDA Graph capture or replay failures when workloads interleave long prefill captures with concurrent decode streams. Failures surface as either: (a) capture abort with CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN during capture for a layer that triggers a different kernel selection at runtime, or (b) replay producing out-of-bounds memory access on tiled KV buffers after allocation growth. This ticket drives a defensive capture lifecycle and a segmented capture approach aligned to attention/kv tiling and fused-attention kernel selection to improve reproducibility and eliminate transient replay correctness issues.
steps_to_reproduce: Launch a mixed prefill + decode workload using batch-size 8 prefill (seq_len 1024) and 32 concurrent single-token decodes on a V100/A100 node.
Enable adaptive kernel selection (fusion heuristics) and on-the-fly quantization profiles.
Run load test for ~30 minutes; observe capture/replay errors in ~0.5-1% of sessions (seen on nightly clusters).
Reproduces reliably when memory pool growth occurs during capture and when two streams capture overlapping kernels without explicit stream ordering.
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: capture nondeterminism arises from two correlated factors: dynamic scratch / workspace size fluctuations (attention fusion chooses larger scratch for some keys) and unordered stream captures that record different kernel pointers/layouts depending on allocation timing.

Observed that fused attention kernels allocate per-call scratch through the memory pool rather than preplanned fixed-size scratch during capture; when the memory pool expands mid-capture, replay expects a different base pointer layout.

CUDA stream capture mode variations (thread-local vs global) change behavior across driver versions; on some nodes the default capture mode allowed concurrent stream captures to interleave their recorded ops, producing nondeterministic graphs.
We ran a controlled repro and captured device logs and device pointers; mismatched base pointers correlate with failure traces.
experiments: Experiment A: Pre-allocate worst-case scratch per attention layer before starting any capture. Result: capture failures dropped from ~0.8% to 0.05%, but memory overhead increased ~6% per model instance.

Experiment B: Scoped capture windows (segmented capture) where each attention block and its downstream KV ops are captured into independent graphs and composed at replay. Result: failures reduced to <0.01% and memory overhead was +1.8%.

Experiment C: Use cudaStreamBeginCapture with cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal on the primary scheduling thread and add explicit stream waits between segments. Result: improved determinism but added 0.4ms median latency per prefill request.
Experiment D: Disabled adaptive kernel selection inside capture (force stable kernel per layer). Result: 0 failures in stress run but regression in some tail latencies for specific prompt shapes.
decision: Adopt segmented capture strategy (Experiment B) combined with a conservative pre-reservation of scratch (small worst-case headroom) for attention fusion to avoid large memory growth during capture. Keep adaptive kernel selection enabled, but add a capture-time override that pins kernel variant if it would change workspace size beyond a threshold.
implementation_plan: 1) Introduce 'segment' abstraction in our capture manager: allow capture boundaries at attention-block granularity and KV flush points.
2) Modify allocator behavior during capture: a lightweight pre-reserve that records fixed base offsets for the duration of current capture segment.

3) Add kernel-selection hook: at capture-time sample kernel metadata and if workspace delta > 10% schedule a pinned kernel for the graph; otherwise allow adaptive selection at replay startup if it does not change recorded pointer layout.
4) Update replay orchestrator to chain segmented graphs with minimal host-side synchronization using stream wait events to preserve ordering without serializing all GPU work.
5) Add unit/integration tests (see test harness entries) and a stress job that runs mixed prefill/decode for 2h in CI-perf cluster.
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind runtime-1.22 flag 'segmented_graph_capture' (off by default).
Canary rollout: enable on 10% of hosted API nodes for 48 hours with capture_retries telemetry and replay-error alerting.
If stable, broaden to 50% then full rollout over two weeks.
Coordinate with Dedicated infra team to snapshot node images for A/B testing across driver versions.
acceptance_criteria: Regression tests added that reproduce previous failures deterministically and assert no failures under segmented capture.
Telemetry shows capture/replay errors drop to <0.02% on canary fleet and tail-latency impact <= +0.5ms for prefill median.
Memory overhead <= +2.5% average per model instance compared to baseline.
No functional regressions on output correctness across evaluated prompt shards.
